# Orientation — the 10-minute tour

ticketd is a ~170-line Flask+SQLite internal ticket tracker, inherited from a contractor
with no git history, no logs, and (for now) no production database. It does four things:
CRUD-lite tickets (create/list/get/close — no edit, no reopen), emails a watchers mailbox
when tickets close, runs a password-reset token flow whose consumer is genuinely unknown
(OQ-002), and has a possibly-dead CSV export from a 2020 audit (OQ-001). The rewrite targets
FastAPI + Postgres and changes exactly three things on purpose — email dispatch becomes
queued (PB-001), reset tokens become CSPRNG-and-hashed (PB-002), and four garbage-input 500s
become 422s — everything else, including the deliberate quirks (200-with-{} on missing
tickets, numeric priority aliases, identical error body for invalid vs expired tokens), is
frozen and replay-checked.

**Trust calibration for this workspace:** every behavioral claim is code-cited, and the
important ones are additionally pinned by golden traces captured from the running legacy app
(T2). What does NOT exist: production traffic evidence (usage weights are structural
guesses), performance envelopes (none invented), and data-census results (queries are ready,
DB access pending — OQ-INT-2). The adversarial audit confirmed 31/35 FIXED claims, and its
two real catches (rate-limit refund semantics, over-broad purge grant) are fixed and
re-verified against the live legacy app.

- Legacy pinned at `tree-02fcc10` (unversioned-snapshot)
- Evidence subsystems: runtime_ingestion=inactive, data_census=inactive, trace_capture_t1=inactive
